overall_summary: Immersive space exploration and extreme exoplanet survival scenarios consistently outperform all other niches on the channel. Videos focusing on bizarre planetary weather (burning ice, supersonic rubies, coal-dark atmospheres) and first-person 'What If' survival concepts drive the highest views and engagement, while cognitive psychology, brain tricks, and simple animal facts struggle to gain traction.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet of Burning Ice' (1,055 views), 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (1,025 views), and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (721 views) represent the channel's peak performance.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on extreme planetary environments, focusing on bizarre chemical compositions, extreme temperatures, and terrifying weather systems.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (959 views) and 'What If You Fell Into This $26 Nonillion Diamond Planet?' (494 views) significantly outperform standard factual listings.
winning_patterns.action: Frame exoplanet discoveries as high-stakes, first-person survival scenarios ('What If You Visited...' or 'What If You Fell Into...') to increase viewer retention.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (stagnating at 10 views) and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' (17 views) consistently fail to find an audience.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standard psychology facts and brain tricks, or completely reframe them through a sci-fi/technological lens.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'The Only Animal That Can Live Forever' generated only 69 views, and 'Sharks Are Older Than WHAT?!' stalled at 122 views.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid basic animal trivia unless it is framed as a high-stakes cinematic survival story or linked to prehistoric/space mysteries.

next_video.concept: What If You Fell Into the Planet That Rains Sideways Glass?
next_video.opening_direction: Show a cinematic, deep-blue alien world with the narrator saying: 'If you stepped onto this beautiful blue planet, you wouldn't drown in water—you'd be shredded by glass flying at 5,000 miles per hour.'
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that because of howling supersonic winds, this glass rain doesn't fall down—it rains entirely sideways, slicing through a space suit in milliseconds.
next_video.reason: Combines the highly successful exoplanet weather theme (HD 189733b) with the top-performing 'What If' first-person survival format to optimize both CTR and retention.

experiment: Test a cinematic AI micro-drama following a fictional astronaut's final 15 seconds on TrES-2b (the coal-dark planet) to see if combining the high-performing exoplanet niche with story-first cinematic tension increases average view duration.
